verdict: Quest Diagnostics grew revenue 10% to $3.1B as test volumes jumped 15%, and wider margins lifted profit attributable to shareholders 28% to $312M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +29% YoY, vs $2.16 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $3.00

kpis.label: Test volume
kpis.note: Requisitions (test orders) rose 14.5%, 14.4% organically; revenue per requisition fell 4.2% on mix

segments.name: Diagnostic Information Services
segments.note: Laboratory testing and the diagnostic insights that come from it, sold to doctors, hospitals, health plans and consumers. 98% of revenue, up 10% YoY.

segments.name: Diagnostic Solutions
segments.note: Risk-assessment services for insurers and healthcare software for providers and payers. The small remainder of revenue, up 2% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling tests and running the company — sales, billing, admin and head office. Up 4% YoY, so it shrank as a share of sales.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Amortization of intangible assets — writing down the value of brands, customer relationships and other intangibles bought in acquisitions, spread over their lives — a bookkeeping charge, not cash.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Small net operating charges, mostly restructuring and integration costs and changes in the value of amounts still owed for past acquisitions.

otherDetail: Other expense was $63M, net: $61M of net interest expense plus $2M of other expense. A separate $9M of equity earnings — Quest's share of profit from joint ventures it part-owns, shown after tax — is the equityM line. The flow uses consolidated net income of $326M; $312M of it was attributable to Quest shareholders after $14M went to noncontrolling interests (partners who own stakes in some Quest businesses).
follow100Note: The other-expense row combines $63M of non-operating expense with $9M of equity earnings from joint ventures, for a net $54M. Profit is the consolidated $326M; $312M of it was attributable to Quest shareholders.

takeaways.title: Volume did the growing
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 10.0% to $3.1B, driven by requisition volume — the number of test orders — up 14.5% (14.4% without acquisitions), across doctors, hospitals and direct-to-consumer channels. Revenue per requisition fell 4.2% on the mix of tests and payers. Quest raised full-year revenue guidance to $12.07B–$12.11B.

takeaways.title: Margins widened as costs grew slowly
takeaways.text: Operating margin — operating profit as a share of revenue — rose to 15.5% from 13.7% a year ago, as operating income jumped 24% to $479M. The cost of running labs rose 10% with volume, but selling and admin costs rose only 4%, helped by automation and AI productivity gains.

takeaways.title: Bottom line rose 28%
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Quest rose 28% to $312M and diluted EPS rose 29% to $2.78. Consolidated net income was $326M, including $14M belonging to noncontrolling interests. Leaving out amortization and small one-off items, Quest's own adjusted EPS was $3.00.

oneTimers: Operating costs include $3M of restructuring and integration charges (workforce reductions and combining bought businesses) and $4M of other charges, mainly an increase in the estimated amount still owed for past acquisitions. Partly offsetting them were about $6M of other gains, including $4M of insurance recoveries for legal matters booked inside selling and admin costs.
footerNote: Quest reports in whole $M. Segment revenues are as reported in the release and the 10-Q (Diagnostic Information Services $3,035M and Diagnostic Solutions $62M).
